info.title: Box+Dice AI API
info.description: Transcribed from the API Blueprint at https://boxdiceaiapi.docs.apiary.io/ by scripts/build-spec.ts. The response side has NOT been verified against a live tenant.

servers.description: Per-tenant. `tenant` is the agency's Box+Dice subdomain; the path segment is whichever partner API the key was provisioned for.

get.summary: List appraisal leads sourced from this integration.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Paging cursor from the previous response's `paging.next` URL. Omit for the first page (oldest records first).

200.description: List appraisal leads sourced from this integration.

204.description: No records newer than the cursor. The body is empty; the caller should wait `Retry-After` seconds and re-request the same URL.

post.summary: Create a sales appraisal or rental BDM lead.
post.description: Idempotent-ish: no new lead is created when an open one already exists for the same contact, property and listing type. When the lead consultant does not have the Lead Flow module enabled this creates a TASK instead — the response `id` is a task id in that case, and nothing in the response says which.

property_id.description: Must be a property owned by the contact.

subject.description: Task subject. Defaults to `New AI Lead`.

task_date.description: Task due date. Defaults to today.

next.description: Absolute URL for the next request, carrying the `after` cursor. Note the API echoes whichever partner path the tenant was provisioned under — the blueprint's own examples show /ai_api/, /aire_api/ and /rebot_api/ — so read the `after` query parameter out of this URL rather than requesting it verbatim.

Paging.description: Cursor block returned by every paginated collection.

id.description: Property ID — the address IS a property record.

Criteria.description: Buying criteria. The blueprint documents this shape twice — once embedded in Contact, once under Search Criteria — and the two lists differ. This is their union; every member is optional, so neither reading is excluded.

status.description: Present ONLY on tombstones: a deleted contact arrives as `{ id, status: "deleted" }` with every other member absent. A sync consumer must branch on this before reading anything else.

Contact.description: A contact. Also used for the per-consultant contact list, which returns the same shape.

active.description: Documented as the attribute; the example instead sends `status`. Both are modelled — expect one of them.

type.description: BUYER_CLOSED, BUYER_IN, BUYER_MAYBE, BUYER_OUT, OWNER, PAST_OWNER, PROS_LANDLORD_APP, PROS_LANDLORD_CAN, PROS_LANDLORD_LISTED, PROS_VENDOR_APP, PROS_VENDOR_CAN, PROS_VENDOR_LISTED, PROS_VENDOR_PRE, PURCHASED, PURCHASER, PURCHASER_CANCELLED, SOLD_BY_OTHER, VENDOR, VENDOR_CANCELLED, VENDOR_SETTLED, VENDOR_SOLD. The /contact_activity_types endpoint also returns BUYER_ENQUIRY, which this list omits — read it from there rather than hard-coding.

Task.description: A task. The completed-tasks endpoint returns the same shape plus `complete_date`; the union is modelled here.

comment.description: The subject line, despite the member name.

cumulative_commission_introduced.description: Documented and observed as a STRING (`"0.0"`), not a number.

name.description: Present in the example, absent from the attribute list.

fixed_price.description: UNRESOLVED: Documented `(Number)`, sent as `false` in the example — the name reads like a flag and the value agrees, but the attribute list does not. Typed as unknown until confirmed against a live response.

amount.description: Present in the example, absent from the attribute list.

percentage.description: Present in the example, absent from the attribute list.

comm_intro_amount.description: Documented and observed as a STRING.

sale_price.description: UNRESOLVED: Documented `(Number)`, sent as the string `"431000.0"`. Typed as unknown until confirmed against a live response.

Voucher.description: The sale and its commission breakdown. This is the richest thing the API exposes and has no equivalent in VaultRE: gross commission, deductions, payment milestones, and per-consultant splits with targets.

ListingFile.description: Public-flagged files only. `url` carries a single-use-looking token query parameter; treat it as short-lived rather than storing it.

status.description: Observed: `settled`. Related activity types imply `VENDOR_SOLD`, `VENDOR_SETTLED`, `SOLD_BY_OTHER` and cancellations elsewhere in the lifecycle; the blueprint never enumerates listing status itself.

auctioneer_id.description: Documented `(Number)`; the example holds a date, which is a copy-paste of `auction_date` rather than a second type. Modelled per the documentation — confirm on capture.

LeadAddress.description: Address as accepted when creating a lead flow lead — used only when `property_id` is unknown. The blueprint types unit/number/postcode as numbers here and as strings everywhere on the read side; both are transcribed as documented rather than reconciled.
